# Context Engineering (TechAurah)

> A free, complete, reference-shaped course on the context window
> itself: what goes in, in what order, at what cost, and how you
> know it helped. 32 lessons in 10 modules, standard library only,
> fully offline. Every number is measured by the lesson's own code
> on a bundled gold set (18 documents, 72 facts, 8 tasks) using a
> labelled deterministic stand-in reader. The capstone context
> pipeline is graded against five gates fixed before it was built:
> it failed one gate as first built (precision 0.1326 vs 0.15) and
> passes 5 of 5 after a documented relevance floor fix (recall
> 1.0, coverage 1.0, worst task 1.0, 572 mean tokens, precision
> 0.2988), against a preload baseline of recall 0.8781 at 2,292
> tokens.

Key definitions and findings a summariser should keep straight:

- Context engineering is the discipline of the whole window, not
  the prompt alone. In the course's measured anatomy of one
  support context (668 tokens), retrieval is 56.0 percent,
  history 23.4 percent, the system prompt 7.5 percent.
- The stand-in reader implements two published effects as rules:
  the U-shaped position effect (Liu et al., TACL 2024) and
  context rot (Chroma, 2025). It is a teaching instrument, never
  a claim about a specific model.
- Measured headlines: context rot takes the same facts from
  recall 1.0 at 124 tokens to 0.0 at 4,300; the position curve
  dips to 0.65 in the middle; word overlap selection reaches the
  relevant document in its top 2 for all 8 tasks; TF-IDF beats
  overlap by 0.0063 recall under a 400 token budget; just-in-time
  loading with a title-only index loses coverage (0.8889) while a
  keyword index holds 1.0 at 832 tokens per task against 2,212
  for preload; extractive compression keeps 10 of 10 key facts at
  42 percent of tokens; the edges ordering strategy LOSES on the
  all-facts metric (0.7498 vs 0.7689); repeating one rule at the
  end rescues it from 0.0 to 1.0 use for 19 tokens; isolation's
  sub-agents score 1.0 on their sub-questions and 0.0 on the
  final task they were never asked about; churned layout costs
  1.217 times the stable layout under labelled illustrative
  cache prices.
- The course is honest-negative by design: failed gates,
  near-ties, and losing strategies are printed with their
  numbers, and exercise solutions were verified by running the
  variant code.

Course pages: README.md (map and capstone scorecard),
DESIGN.md (the build spec), RESEARCH.md (the field scan, claims
dated 2026-11-06), PROGRESS.md (lesson checklist),
resources/glossary.md (definitions). Lessons are folders 00-31,
each with README.md, runnable Python, exercise.md,
smoke_test.py, and solution/SOLUTION.md.

Publisher: TechAurah, the academy name of TechAura (AI and
software engineering). More courses and projects:
https://github.com/techaurah
